stem.en: An altitude meets the opposite line at which angle?

whyWrong.en: An altitude is perpendicular to the line.
An altitude is perpendicular to the line.

explanation.en: An altitude is perpendicular to the line.

stem.en: Which side is opposite C in triangle ABC?

whyWrong.en: AB is the side that does not contain C.
AB is the side that does not contain C.

explanation.en: AB is the side that does not contain C.

stem.en: Where is the foot of an altitude?

text.en: Where the perpendicular meets the opposite line

whyWrong.en: The foot is the intersection on the base line.

text.en: At the midpoint of every side

whyWrong.en: The foot is the intersection on the base line.

explanation.en: The foot is the intersection on the base line.

stem.en: What should you do if the perpendicular misses the base segment?

text.en: Tilt the perpendicular to touch the segment

whyWrong.en: The altitude may meet the extension at 90°.
The altitude may meet the extension at 90°.

text.en: Extend the base as a straight line

explanation.en: The altitude may meet the extension at 90°.

stem.en: How many altitudes does a triangle have?

whyWrong.en: Use each of the three vertices in turn.
Use each of the three vertices in turn.

explanation.en: Use each of the three vertices in turn.

stem.en: A right triangle has a right angle at B. What is the altitude from A to the line BC?

whyWrong.en: AB already meets BC at a right angle.
AB already meets BC at a right angle.

explanation.en: AB already meets BC at a right angle.

stem.en: Which triangle can have an altitude outside its boundary?

whyWrong.en: The base extension may be needed in an obtuse triangle.
The base extension may be needed in an obtuse triangle.

explanation.en: The base extension may be needed in an obtuse triangle.

stem.en: Two lines from C reach AB. One makes 70°, the other 90°. Which is the altitude?

whyWrong.en: An altitude is the perpendicular segment from the vertex.
An altitude is the perpendicular segment from the vertex.

explanation.en: An altitude is the perpendicular segment from the vertex.
